title: CIC agent tricks Schauberger into signing his work over; IP ends up at Brookhaven
summary: Jesse Michels tells of CIC agent tricks Schauberger into signing his work over; IP ends up at Brookhaven, about post-1945 at Europe; Brookhaven National Lab, Long Island, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Europe; Brookhaven National Lab, Long Island

tellings.quote: After the war ended, another Army CIC agent, Neil Gershimer, tricked Shawberger into signing all of his work over to the United States.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that after the Second World War ended in 1945, an agent of the US Army's Counter Intelligence Corps named Neil Gershimer tricked a European inventor, Viktor Schauberger, into signing all his work over to the United States. According to Michels, those ideas and inventions ended up at Brookhaven National Laboratory, a US government research lab on Long Island. If true, it would mean unusual wartime technology quietly passed into American hands.
